Senses.Explanation: Literally, 'raise or present in full.' The expression occurs 1,834 times in 308 allowlisted texts. Chan records contrast it with a half-presentation: one discourse says that seeing no single form is only 'half presented' (半提) and that one must still know a time of full presentation. It regularly modifies a saying or command. Records ask how to speak 'one saying fully presented' (一句全提), pair it with 'the ancestral master's true command' (祖師正令), and call the flower at Vulture Peak and the snow at Shaoshi the separate transmission personally shown and the true command fully presented. Thus the Chan deployment is not merely completeness in the abstract: it is an utterance, command, or teaching-seat presentation brought forward without remainder. The texts also use the fixed compounds 'the true command fully presented' (全提正令) and 'a single saying fully presented' (一句全提).
Senses.Note: No second referent or word-class emerged. Uses with command, saying, and presentation are deployment shapes of the same act, not separate things.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: A discourse supplies the explicit contrast: even seeing no single form is only half-presentation; the following sentence requires knowing a time of full presentation.
The discourse pairs full presentation across past and present with the ancestral master's true command.

Occurrences.Kwic: 格外全提一句作麼生道
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A monk asks how to speak a single beyond-rank saying in full.

Occurrences.Kwic: 靈山花發，親示別傳；少室雪寒，全提正令
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A teaching-seat discourse joins the Vulture Peak flower, Shaoshi snow, separate transmission, and the true command fully presented.
A recorded discourse says that when one saying is fully presented, the thousand differences gather together.

Senses.Explanation: Literally ‘whole or complete’ (全) + ‘trigger, pivot, or dynamic’ (機): the whole dynamic or full pivotal function. The compound has 843 occurrences in 224 allowlisted texts. It is especially visible in ‘the whole dynamic and great function’ (全機大用), with 115 occurrences in 60 texts. Yuanwu says this ‘whole dynamic and great function is manifest wherever one touches’ (全機大用觸處見成); elsewhere his record says ‘as the grass bends and the wind moves, the whole dynamic alone is exposed’ (草偃風行全機獨露), then asks what one says without relying on any thing or phrase. ‘The whole dynamic alone exposed’ (全機獨露) occurs 21 times in 19 texts; ‘the whole dynamic thoroughly freed’ (全機透脫) occurs 5 times in 5; and ‘the whole dynamic alone functioning’ (全機獨用) occurs twice in 2. The Blue Cliff Record uses it both in the rubric ‘the whole dynamic is displayed everywhere’ (全機隨處齊彰) and in its comment that several actions are all ‘places of the whole dynamic and great function’ (全機大用處). A lamp-record master also uses the compound predicatively: ‘if I deploy the whole dynamic, where will you search?’ (我若全機，汝向甚麼處摸索). These attested combinations supply the article's wording; the corpus gives no formula equating the compound with a further noun.
Senses.Note: The one hit for ‘whole dynamic + one who’ (全機者) occurs in ‘one who broadly displayed the whole dynamic’ (廓顯全機者); the final graph nominalizes the person and does not define the term. The one question ‘what is the whole dynamic?’ (如何是全機) receives the recorded answer ‘in the dead of night, the sun is bright’ (半夜日頭明); the record supplies no explanatory gloss, and this entry adds none. The same corpus-wide wording spans direct discourse, case rubrics, verse, and prose comment, so no master-specific key or second sense is warranted.

Occurrences.Kwic: 全機大用觸處見成。溢目清光貫通今古。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Yuanwu's own record, first formal address: ‘the whole dynamic and great function is manifest wherever one touches; clear light filling the eyes passes through past and present.’

Occurrences.Kwic: 草偃風行全機獨露。正當恁麼時不依倚一物一句作麼生道。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Yuanwu's own record, fourth formal address: ‘as grass bends and wind moves, the whole dynamic alone is exposed; just then, without relying on one thing or one phrase, what do you say?’

Occurrences.Kwic: 直下更無纖翳。全機隨處齊彰。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Blue Cliff Record, case-pointer rubric: ‘directly there is not the slightest screen; the whole dynamic is displayed everywhere.’ Editorial rubric rather than an encounter speaker, so MasterName is null.

Occurrences.Kwic: 上堂。我若全機。汝向甚麼處摸索。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Wudeng huiyuan, Fuzhou Baoguo Zhao section: in a formal address the master says, ‘if I deploy the whole dynamic, where will you search?’ The section master is not linked through the roster.

Occurrences.Kwic: 雖然總是全機大用處。俱不如禾山解打鼓。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Blue Cliff Record prose comment: ‘although all are places of the whole dynamic and great function, none equals Heshan's “knows how to beat the drum.”’ Editorial comment comparing recorded actions, so MasterName is null.

Senses.Explanation: Literally, the entire body. The term occurs 1,418 times in 299 allowlisted texts and ranges grammatically from a noun ('fall short of the whole') to an extent expression ('entirely is the pearl'); these describe the same thing as a complete whole rather than different referents. Its characteristic Chan collocations make that whole 'appear' (378 hits in 174 texts) or be 'exposed' (153 in 95). Xuansha's pearl exchange says, 'the whole body is the pearl—who else would you have recognize it?' Teaching-seat verses pair a raised whisk, staff, dust mote, or opened sleeve with the whole body's appearing.
Senses.Note: The different grammatical placements do not warrant a split: noun, modifier, and extent readings all designate completeness of the same referent. The deviation lies in the recurring public formulas 'the whole body appears' (全體現) and 'the whole body is exposed' (全體露), not in an imported claim about a metaphysical 'total reality.'

Occurrences.Kwic: 既是一顆明珠，學人為甚不識？沙曰：全體是珠，更教誰識？
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Xuansha's recorded pearl exchange predicates the whole body as the pearl.

Occurrences.Kwic: 極目青天無片雲，萬象森羅全體露。若也擬議更商量，特地翻成箇露布。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A teaching-seat verse uses the recurrent 'whole body exposed' formula.

Occurrences.Kwic: 舉拂子云。盧舍本身全體現。當機直下沒纖毫。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The whole body's appearance is spoken while the master raises the whisk.

Occurrences.Kwic: 驀拈拄杖云：「龍袖拂開全體現，象王行處絕狐蹤。」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A master raises the staff and quotes the recurring whole-body-appears line.

Occurrences.Kwic: 當機微笑，窺見一斑；依位無言，猶虧全體。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: An interview question contrasts seeing one patch with falling short of the whole.
